item.title: Powerful quake shakes Panama, canal operations normal
item.description: The quake was reportedly felt in the capital, Panama City, as well as in the capital of neighbouring Costa Rica.

People holding babies stand outside the maternity ward of a hospital in Panama City on Oct 9, following a magnitude 7.7 earthquake. PHOTO: AFP

Set as preferred source

Listen Summarise

A 7.7 magnitude earthquake struck near Panama’s southern coast at a 10km depth, the US Geological Survey said, and people were seen evacuating buildings in Panama City. No damage was first reported, and the Panama Canal Authority said canal operations were normal after the quake. The US Tsunami Warning System warned of possible hazardous waves for Panama and several Pacific countries, and said Hawaii also faced a tsunami threat.

AI generated

PANAMA CITY - A strong 7.7 magnitude earthquake struck near the southern coast of Panama on Oct 9 at a 10km depth, according to the US Geological Survey, yet no damage was initially reported and the Panama Canal Authority said the waterway was operating normally. Panama television footage showed people evacuating buildings. The quake’s epicentre was close to the rural community of La Pitaloza in a sparsely populated area in the south of the country, close to the country’s Pacific coastline.

The impact prompted the US Tsunami Warning System to warn that hazardous tsunami waves were possible along parts of the coasts of Panama, Colombia, Costa Rica, Ecuador, Peru, Nicaragua, Guatemala, El Salvador, and Mexico within the next three hours. The system also said there was a tsunami threat to Hawaii. The quake was felt in the capital, Panama City, as well as in the capital of neighbouring Costa Rica, according to Reuters witnesses. REUTERS
